title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
On Tuesday, New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators, each about the size of a tractor trailer, at its Vineland data center site in late July. None of the 2,000 kilowatt generators had permits to be installed or operated. State officials said the penalty for violating the Air Pollution Control Act is the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey. The campus is under construction and is planned to be 2.6 million square feet, use 350 megawatts, and be completed at the end of the year. Some parts are already in use.

The project has drawn complaints since the zoning process, including a federal lawsuit by homeowners over ongoing noise. The Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders to DataOne for too much noise. Governor Mikie Sherrill said at a Climate Week event that building data centers must benefit New Jersey communities.
